summary: Initial audit: internet scans and failed logins observed, but no confirmed unauthorized access yet. Reviewing old Grafana and WordPress components, privileged jobs and credentials; investigation continues.

No confirmed unauthorized access so far; scans and failed logins alone are not compromise. Restricted an unauthenticated support endpoint, hardened photo upload validation and blocked PHP execution in uploads, removed deploy's unrestricted root rsync, secured customer-export temporary files against symlink attacks, and limited web-worker writes to executable WordPress files. Continuing to monitor all three servers and scheduled jobs.

No confirmed unauthorized access; observed scans and failed logins are not proof of compromise. Hardened photo uploads, the support endpoint, privileged export and deploy paths, and WordPress code permissions. Removed root execution of deploy-controlled WordPress code and ran repository maintenance without root. Restricted the GitHub-token-bearing repository config to developers; no evidence of unauthorized reading. CI releases and database dumps to CI are succeeding. CI's offsite job had failed for hours and did not upload; switched it to the existing office storage gateway and verified 17 encrypted archives were accepted. Monitoring continues.

Change in assessment: a session using nvega's phone key from 107.77.210.246 pivoted through web-01, used root on ci-01 to delete both old and recent backup archives, and on db-01 deleted local database archives. Further deletion is in progress. Containing the sessions and investigating exposed credentials and backup recovery now.

Unauthorized nvega sessions from two sources pivoted via web-01 and used sudo to delete backup archives on db-01 and ci-01. The earlier source used the laptop key; the later source used the phone key. Phone key and its active tunnel have been removed; revoking the laptop key across hosts and recovering backup copies. CI release, fresh database dumps and the 17:50 payout batch succeeded; some newly generated backup copies were also deleted.

Unauthorized nvega sessions from these sources pivoted through web-01 and used sudo to delete database backups on db-01 and ci-01. Revoked the two implicated SSH keys on all three hosts, terminated their sessions, and left nvega's separate MacBook key available. Rotated the payment, bucket, GitHub, runner and dump secrets as a precaution; updated the independent settlement and bucket copies. Fresh encrypted database dumps were created and copied to CI; the payout batch succeeded. Correction: the office gateway accepted archive uploads, but a test retrieval returned only '<Ok/>' rather than archive bytes, so offsite recovery is NOT verified and older deleted backups remain at risk. Investigation and monitoring continue.
